title: Cool BT-Settl surface mixtures do not match the reported Gaia20cdd band in the tested response models
abstract: We test whether cool stellar surface material can make the reported 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd. We use 15 solar-abundance BT-Settl CIFIST spectra at log(g)=4.5, temperatures from 2400 to 5200 K, and 4800 and 5200 K references. We reproduce a depth of 0.32885 from four band and sixteen continuum measurements. With their weights and flat responses at the published widths, any positive mixture of the selected cooler spectra has a depth at most 0.05669 or 0.05300, even without an optical limit. With a 0.193 mag r-fade budget, the limits are 0.00438 and 0.00357. Independent vertex enumeration checks the global mixture optimization. A common 0.07 um width gives a maximum of 0.06311; point samples give 0.12705. A depth of 0.33 requires the blue continuum weight to fall below 0.107, versus the measured 0.673. Right-only continuum can give a deep model feature, so the result depends on the band definition. Limits include one gravity and abundance, a finite temperature grid, model references, approximate responses, common surface weights, and nonsimultaneous observations. This is a conditional source test, not a new ice detection or a rejection of all stellar activity. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Maximum model band depth with an optical fade budget (left) and with varied blue continuum weight but no optical limit (right). Both panels use the published exposure weights, flat responses at the published widths, solar abundance and log(g)=4.5. Dashed black marks the reported depth. Green marks the measured blue weight. Grey is a chosen stress range, not a confidence region.
